data.name: AppName
data.comment: Window title and message box caption. Usually left untranslated.

data.name: WindowTitle
data.comment: {0} = "*" when unsaved, {1} = file or marina name, {2} = AppName.

data.name: UnsavedMarker
data.comment: Put in front of the title while there are unsaved changes.

data.name: NewMarinaName
data.comment: Name a brand-new design starts with.

data.name: DefaultFileName
data.comment: Used when the marina name has no characters a file name can keep.

data.name: ToolLandTip
data.value: Draw a quay, a lawn or a breakwater

data.name: ToolPierTip
data.value: Draw a pier out from the shore

data.name: ToolBerthsTip
data.value: Fill a stretch of pier with berths

data.name: ToolAshoreTip
data.value: Place berths ashore, for boats kept out of the water

data.name: CommandTopViewTip
data.value: Look straight down with north up (Ctrl+T)

data.name: StatusCamera
data.comment: {0} = distance to the camera target, {1} = tilt above the horizon.

data.name: StatusPointer
data.comment: Position of the pointer in plan coordinates.

data.name: LogEntry
data.comment: {0} = time, {1} = the message.

data.name: LogNewMarina
data.value: New marina. Load a reference image to trace the real shape, or start with the land tool.

data.name: LogAddedLand
data.comment: {0} = land area name, {1} = number of corners, {2} = area.

data.name: LogAddedPier
data.comment: {0} = pier name, {1} = length, {2} = width.

data.name: LogAddedBerth
data.comment: {0} = berth name.

data.name: LogAddedBerths
data.comment: {0} = count, {1} = the berth names.

data.name: LogRemoved
data.comment: {0} = what was removed, {1} and {2} = what went with it.

data.name: LogTrees
data.comment: {0} = land area name, {1} = trees now, {2} = trees before.

data.name: LogUndone
data.comment: {0} = description of the undone step.

data.name: LogScaleLine
data.value: Scale line drawn: {0:0.0} m at the current image scale

data.name: LogReferenceImage
data.comment: {0} = what changed, {1} = the scale.

data.name: LogRendererError
data.comment: {0} = the error message.

data.name: LogOpened
data.comment: {0} = file name, {1} and {2} = what it holds.

data.name: LogOpenedNewerVersion
data.comment: Appended to LogOpened. {0} = that file’s format version.

data.name: LogSaved
data.comment: {0} = file name, {1} = number of berths.

data.name: LogImageLoaded
data.value: Loaded {0}. Draw a line over something of a known length, then type that length.
data.comment: {0} = file name.

data.name: LogFailed
data.comment: {0} = what failed, {1} = the reason.

data.name: OpenImageTitle
data.value: Top-down image of the marina (north at the top)

data.name: OpenFailed
data.value: The design could not be opened

data.name: SaveFailed
data.value: The design could not be saved

data.name: ImageLoadFailed
data.value: The image could not be loaded

data.name: WarnBody
data.comment: {0} = what failed, {1} = the reason.

data.name: ConfirmDiscard
data.comment: {0} = file or marina name.

data.name: ShortcutsBody
data.value:
Mouse Left drag pan the view Right drag orbit Wheel zoom Click use the tool in hand Right click finish a shape (land area), or clear the trees under it
Keys Esc cancel what you are drawing, then back to Navigate Enter finish the land area you are drawing Backspace take back the last corner Delete remove what the eraser points at Ctrl+Z undo the last change Shift (while drawing) snap a pier or a bow direction to 15° steps Alt (while drawing) ignore the snapping to corners and edges
data.comment: Keep the columns lined up when translating.

data.name: AboutBody
data.comment: {0} = application name, {1} = its version, {2} = the library version, {3} = the graphics backend, {4} = the .NET runtime, {5} = year, {6} = author.

data.name: ToolLookTip
data.value: Water, light, colours and labels, with the marina still live beside them

data.name: LookHint
data.value: Change how the marina is drawn. The view stays live, so you can turn and zoom while you work.

data.name: ResetTip
data.comment: Tooltip on the small reset button beside a setting.

data.name: ResetGlyph
data.comment: The reset button face. A symbol, not words; leave it as it is.

data.name: LandRockVariationTip
data.value: How much single rocks differ in brightness from one another.

data.name: LabelFaceTip
data.value: Weight and width of the lettering painted on the water.

data.name: PreviewFillTip
data.value: How many of the berths get a boat when you press Add boats.

data.name: PreviewHint
data.value: Boats to judge the settings against. They are never saved with the design — the host application decides who is in the marina.

data.name: LogPreviewBoats
data.value: Put {0} preview boats in the marina
data.comment: {0} = how many.

data.name: LandSurfaceTip
data.value: What the area is made of. Lawns can have trees on them.

data.name: LandHeightTip
data.value: How far the surface stands above the water.

data.name: LandHint
data.value: Click each corner in the view, then press Enter (or click the first corner) to close the shape.

data.name: PierConstructionTip
data.value: Floating pontoon or fixed concrete pier; it sets the deck height and the look.

data.name: PierBerthsTip
data.value: A pier along a quay wall or a mole only takes boats on its water side.

data.name: PierHint
data.value: Click the shore end, then the far end. The pier squares up with the quay and the piers already there — hold Alt to draw it at any angle, Shift for 15° steps.

data.name: PierNameTip
data.value: Name given to each new pier. {pier} stands for its letter, so "Pier {pier}" gives "Pier A".

data.name: BerthWidthTip
data.value: Across the berth: the widest boat that fits.

data.name: BerthLengthTip
data.value: Away from the pier: the longest boat that fits.

data.name: BerthDepthTip
data.value: Water depth, stored as the berth's maximum draft.

data.name: AlignBerths
data.value: Continue the row already on that side

data.name: BerthServicesTip
data.value: Power and water points, placed between every two berths of the pier.

data.name: BerthHint
data.value: Click beside a pier where the row starts, then where it ends. Clear the tick above to start the row exactly where you click.

data.name: SeparatorHintFingerPiers
data.value: Each berth gets its own pair of short finger piers.

data.name: SeparatorHintNone
data.value: Nothing between the berths but a gap, so boats lie side by side.

data.name: SeparatorHintFingerPier
data.value: One walkable pier between every two berths.

data.name: SeparatorHintPiles
data.value: A row of mooring piles between every two berths.

data.name: SeparatorHintBoom
data.value: A floating boom between every two berths.

data.name: SeparatorHintPaired
data.value: A pier every other berth: each boat has a pier on one side and a neighbour on the other.

data.name: SeparatorHintSinglePile
data.value: One mooring pile at the outer end of every berth boundary (Mediterranean mooring).

data.name: SeparatorHintSpacing
data.value: Berths are {0:0.##} m apart, {1:0.##} m from center to center.
data.comment: Appended to the separator hint. {0} = gap, {1} = spacing.

data.name: BerthNamePatternTip
data.value: Name of each new berth. {pier} is the pier, {pierName} its name, {side} the side (L or R) and {number} the running number.

data.name: BerthStartNumberTip
data.value: Number the first new berth gets. Names already taken are skipped, so a second row carries on after the first.

data.name: BerthIncrementTip
data.value: Step from one berth to the next: 1 gives 1, 2, 3; 2 gives 1, 3, 5.

data.name: BerthNamingExample
data.comment: {0} = the first few names the scheme would give.

data.name: LandBerthHeadingTip
data.value: Direction the stored boat faces: 0° = north, 90° = east.

data.name: LandNamePatternTip
data.value: Name of each new slot ashore. {pier} is the land area, {pierName} its name and {number} the running number.

data.name: LandStartNumberTip
data.value: Number the first new slot ashore gets. Counts separately from the berths on the water.

data.name: LandBerthHint
data.value: Click the spot on a land area, then click where the bow should point. Click the same spot twice to use the direction above.

data.name: TreeNone
data.comment: Shown on the coverage slider at zero.

data.name: TreeHint
data.value: Trees per 1000 m². Click a lawn to scatter them; click again for a different arrangement, Ctrl+click (or right-click) to clear it.

data.name: EraseHint
data.value: Click a berth, a pier or a land area to remove it. Piers and land areas take their berths with them, and berths take the separators that only served them.

data.name: EraseUndoHint
data.value: Ctrl+Z brings back anything you remove by mistake.

data.name: SelectHint
data.value: Drag a box over the water. Every berth whose middle falls inside it is selected; hold Shift or Ctrl to add to the ones already selected.

data.name: SelectCount
data.comment: {0} = how many.

data.name: ServicesHint
data.value: Pick what the pedestals offer, then click a berth. Hold Alt or Ctrl to change every berth down that side of the pier.

data.name: ServicesInheritHint
data.value: A berth left alone takes whatever its pier offers, so only the ones you change carry their own setting.

data.name: RenameHint
data.value: Click a berth to give it another name, or a pier to give it a title. Berth names are also their ids, so each one must be free.

data.name: RenameUndoHint
data.value: Ctrl+Z puts the old name back.

data.name: RenameBerthQuestion
data.value: What should this berth be called?

data.name: RenamePierQuestion
data.value: What should this pier be called?

data.name: RenamePierIdQuestion
data.value: Its id, which its berths and dividers point at:

data.name: LogPierIdChanged
data.comment: {0} = the old id, {1} = the new one.

data.name: ToolServicesTip
data.value: Give berths power and water; Alt or Ctrl changes a whole side of a pier

data.name: ToolSelectTip
data.value: Drag a box over the water to select the berths inside it

data.name: ToolRenameTip
data.value: Rename a berth or a pier

data.name: RenameTakenBody
data.value: {0} is already used by something else in this marina. Pick another.
data.comment: {0} = the name that is taken.

data.name: LogRenamed
data.comment: {0} = the old name, {1} = the new one.

data.name: LogRenameRefused
data.value: {0} is already taken; {1} keeps its name.
data.comment: {0} = the name asked for, {1} = the berth.

data.name: ToolCoastTip
data.value: Draw the coast of the mainland behind the marina

data.name: CoastSceneryTip
data.value: What is scattered across the land behind the shore. Bare ground is the cheapest to draw.

data.name: CoastHint
data.value: Click along the coast (two points make a straight one), press Enter, then click the side that is land.

data.name: CoastEndlessHint
data.value: The first and last stretches run on without end, so the land never stops however far you pull back.

data.name: CoastNone
data.value: No mainland: the marina stands in open water.

data.name: CoastPresent
data.comment: {0} = how many points the coast has, {1} = the cover, e.g. "Countryside".

data.name: LogCoastDrawn
data.comment: {0} = how many points the coast has.

data.name: TrafficShowTip
data.value: Boats, yachts and a ferry crossing the bay beyond the marina. They are decoration: they cannot be clicked and take no berth.

data.name: TrafficIntensityTip
data.value: How many vessels are out there at once.

data.name: TrafficClearanceTip
data.value: How near the middle of the marina the shipping passes. Turn the path on below to see where it runs.

data.name: TrafficSpeedTip
data.value: How fast the vessels cross, in knots.

data.name: TrafficPasses
data.value: {0} lane(s); the nearest passes {1} m from the middle of the marina.
data.comment: {0} = how many lanes, {1} = closest approach in whole meters.

data.name: TrafficNoRoom
data.value: No lane could be found: lower the clearance, or widen the water.

data.name: TrafficHint
data.value: The lanes follow the coast past the marina, each running the opposite way to its neighbours. Vessels fade in and away far out to sea.

data.name: TrafficLanesTip
data.value: How many lanes of shipping there are. The nearest passes at the distance below, and the rest step out to sea from it.

data.name: TrafficLaneSpacingTip
data.value: How far apart the lanes are. It also sets how far a vessel may wander across its own lane, so wider lanes look looser.

data.name: TrafficShowLanesTip
data.value: Draws the lines the shipping follows, tinted by which way each one runs, so the spacing can be set by eye. It is not saved with the design.

data.name: ValueKnots
data.comment: {0} = speed in knots.

data.name: ToolCamerasTip
data.value: Saved views of the marina, and which of the automatic ones to offer

data.name: CamerasHint
data.value: Pick a view to go there. Untick one to leave it out of the list the host application offers.

data.name: CameraNameTip
data.value: What to call the view you are looking at now.

data.name: CameraSaveHint
data.value: Saves where the camera is now, so you and the host application can come back to it.

data.name: CameraGoToGlyph
data.comment: Face of the go-to-this-view button. A symbol, not words; leave it as it is.

data.name: CameraGoToTip
data.value: Move the camera to this view

data.name: CameraDeleteGlyph
data.comment: Face of the delete-this-view button. A symbol, not words; leave it as it is.

data.name: CameraDefaultName
data.comment: {0} = a number, to make a name up when the box is empty.

data.name: LogCameraSaved
data.comment: {0} = the view name.

data.name: LogCameraDeleted
data.comment: {0} = the view name.

data.name: LogCameraDisabled
data.comment: {0} = the view name.

data.name: LogCameraEnabled
data.comment: {0} = the view name.

data.name: ShadowsShowTip
data.value: The boats and the piers throw their shape onto the water and the quays. Turning it off makes a big marina cheaper to draw.

data.name: ShadowStrengthTip
data.value: How dark a shadow is. Past about 40% the places where a boat overlaps its own shadow start to show.

data.name: ShadowHint
data.value: Shadows follow the sun above. They land on the ground an object stands over, so a boat ashore shades the yard rather than the water.

data.name: WaterAreaTip
data.value: How far out the water has waves, reflections and glints. Past it the sea carries on flat to the horizon, which costs nothing to draw.

data.name: TrafficMaximumTip
data.value: The most vessels on the water at once. How busy is a share of this.

data.name: ValueVessels
data.comment: {0} = how many.

data.name: ValueLanes
data.comment: {0} = how many.

data.name: ImageClearScaleLineTip
data.value: Removes the measuring line once the picture is scaled. The line is never saved with the design.

data.name: ImageStateEmpty
data.value: Load a top-down photo or map of the marina (north up) and set its scale, then trace over it.

data.name: ImageStateLine
data.value: The line you drew is {0:0.0} m long at the current scale. Type what it should be and apply.

data.name: ImageStateReady
data.value: Image is {0:0} × {1:0} m ({2:0.###} m per pixel). Draw a line over a known length to set the scale.

data.name: Percent
data.comment: {0} = a whole percentage.

data.name: Summary
data.value: {0} berth(s): {1} on the water, {2} ashore {3} pier(s), {4} land area(s), {5} separator(s), {6} tree(s) {7:0} × {8:0} m overall
data.comment: Counts of everything drawn, then the overall size.

data.name: ValueMetersWhole
data.comment: {0} = a whole number of meters.

data.name: BoatMovementHint
data.value: How much moored boats, buoys and booms rise, fall and roll with the waves.

data.name: ValueMeters
data.comment: {0} = a length in meters.

data.name: ValueTimes
data.comment: A multiplier, e.g. ×1.5.

data.name: ValueStill
data.comment: Shown at zero on the wave speed and boat movement sliders.
